item.title: Five Years of Swapped Circuits: an Afternoon with Claude to Put My Heat Pump the Right Way Round
item.description: A circulation pump set to a fixed 100% since day one, a mixing valve stuck at 100%, a sensor strapped onto plastic pipe, and above all two circuits swapped in the controller. How we proved it with two switches and Home Assistant’s history, what we changed (heating curves, the floor’s maximum water temperature, the radio thermostat IDs), what it gave, and the three fixes the Home Assistant integration got along the way.

item.title: Who Is Really Using My Fibre? Mirroring Every Packet to a Raspberry Pi with ntopng
item.description: A follow-up to the home network monitoring post. Why per-port counters weren’t enough, why the switch must be able to mirror a port, why the Pi must be a 4 or newer with real Gigabit Ethernet and a second interface, how to cable it so every device crosses the mirrored link, how to configure the switch, the listen-only interface, ntopng and softflowd, what ntopng shows per device, and how six speed tests showed that the mystery traffic most likely lives only in the ISP box’s own counter. Every name, address and identifier is pseudonymized.

item.title: Have You Tried Turning It Off and On Again? Monitoring a Home Network So You Know What Broke
item.description: A mini PC, Uptime Kuma, OpenObserve and Home Assistant watching a home network. What each layer catches, the reset that “fixed” the Wi-Fi and hid 2–3 TB a day of mystery traffic, the reboot that took every public service down, a map of which Wi-Fi device sits on which mesh unit, and a live debugging session where Claude solved a “client stuck without an IP” alert by correlating two data sources. Every name, address and identifier is pseudonymized.

item.title: One Year Later: I Asked a Stronger Model to Review My Vibe-Coded App
item.description: I built Cyber Code Academy in December 2025 with Cursor and Copilot, and had the AI of the time check its security. One year later, a single prompt to Claude Opus 5.5 found 50 problems, two of them critical. Anyone could delete the challenges, and any learner could fake their own test results. The bugs, the fixes, the redesign, and a second prompt that showed the exercises were unfair too.

item.title: Home Assistant Ships Every Month: a CI That Reads the Release Notes, Opens an Issue and Waits for a Label
item.description: A bug report led me to a nightly check that had been green for weeks while twelve tests failed. The new CI has three layers. Deterministic checks that really fail, a Claude review of each Home Assistant monthly release posted as an issue (about $1.17 a run), and a label that asks Claude to open a fix PR with six narrow tools. The diagrams, the security model, the first real review, and a narrated video.
